title: ToolVision: Learning When and How to Use Visual Tools with Capability-Aligned Supervision

rs.innovation_approach: heterogeneous_decomposition (primary): fixed question tiers receive different tool-success bonuses; decompose_and_delegate (supporting): student delegates localization/OCR/counting to specialist tools through code and returned images; self_supervised_signal_engineering (supporting): generated answer outcomes manufacture otherwise missing step-utility and tool-need labels, with existing task GT still required.
rs.key_step: First seed student-usable executed trajectories using a cross-scale committee; then measure frozen-SFT no-tool/tool-enabled outcomes offline and gate a successful-tool trajectory bonus by fixed question tier.
rs.why_non_obvious: A strong teacher can emit accurate crop coordinates that a smaller student cannot reproduce. Low answer accuracy alone confounds tool-responsive questions with questions neither route can solve. Executable calls can still miss the relevant pixels.
rs.trigger_condition: When teacher demonstrations and blanket tool rewards misalign with student ability, filter evidence using student-scale judges and condition tool bonuses on frozen-model rollout groups; test whether this transfers to the evolving policy.
reviewer_praise: low_evidence: no local OpenReview reviews supplied
reviewer_concern: low_evidence: no reviewer text; limitations below are source statements or reader analysis
rs.acceptance_signal: Local arXiv v1 dated 9 Aug 2026; manifest decision null; no acceptance inference.
rs.abstract_strategy: Partition examples by measured response to an available intervention and apply distinct incentives; route weak capabilities through structured specialist outputs.
rs.abstract_key_step: Reject generated demonstrations that lose measured answerability, retain a bounded neutral bridge, and reuse a frozen intervention-response label to gate later reward.
rs.abstract_why_non_obvious: Demonstration success under a strong producer does not imply imitable success under the learner, and difficulty is not intervention benefit.
rs.abstract_trigger_condition: When demonstrations exceed learner capacity and uniform incentives encourage unhelpful actions, measure learner-scale outcomes before tailoring the treatment.

question.load_bearing_assumption: Correct strong-teacher trajectories are directly imitable by small students, and successful tool use is beneficial uniformly across questions.
question.scope: Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking with heterogeneous code-based image tools, supervised initialization plus fixed-label GSPO; not solely caption+crop and not per-call credit.
question.success_criterion: Improve benchmark accuracy with more targeted specialist use relative to same-pool distilledSFT and uniform bonus. Author supplies no preregistered noninferiority/overall cost-reduction criterion.
question.why_open: Outcome rewards can suppress unreliable tool execution, blanket bonuses reward irrelevant valid calls; task difficulty or teacher success fails to identify student-usable evidence.
